quotes.text: The church of S.Ivo alla Sapienza stands inside the small courtyard of the Palazzo della Sapienza, the ancient University of Rome from the 15th century until 1935 when it became the seat of the State Archive.
quotes.page: Turismo Roma, Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, opening line

quotes.text: On the attic, stands the multifoiled dome. On the top, the original clerestory with a spiral cusp, travertine torches, culminating in a crown, on which, made of wrought iron,  are a sphere, a cross and a dove with the olive branch in its beak.
quotes.page: Turismo Roma, Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, dome paragraph

quotes.text: The church’s interior, due to the busy plan and the surge of the pilaster strips, continued from the dome into six segments, all in light colours, is even more surprising for the innovations in concepts and decorations.
quotes.page: Turismo Roma, Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, interior paragraph

measurements.name: dome_segment_count
measurements.as_printed: continued from the dome into six segments
measurements.note: Six lobes, which is the same figure as the Italian version's 'stella a sei punte' and is the geometric consequence of the node's own claim that the plan comes from two superimposed equilateral triangles.

note: Tranche 3, the antique orders cluster, 5 Sep 2026. The register corroborates the node's generative claim without asserting it: the node says the plan is 'generated from two superimposed equilateral triangles' and the register says the centralised plan draws 'a sort of six-pointed star' and that the walls follow its perimeter. Six is the only number in the record.
